findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a significant number of drain flies present at the floor drain under the pretzel prep table. The PIC was aware of the issue and is in contact with Orkin. A follow-up will be conducted in one month (June 26, 2026) to ensure the pest concern has been resolved. Maintain pest control receipts for inspector to view.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed PIC of staff to have no certified food protection manager (CFPM) certification. PIC stated she has been out on medical leave and plans to take the course soon. Ensure there is a CFPM on staff at all times during operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink. The faucet of the hand sink is touched with dirty hands, and therefore poses a cross-contamination hazard. Ensure staff are using a barrier such as a paper towel to turn off the hand sink to avoid cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed no food handler’s certification on file for employees in the facility. There was one certification on the wall which was expired. Ensure staff are obtaining their food handler’s certification within 30 days of hire and all certificates are available for view.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed 2 sanitizing solution buckets at front counter to test at 0 ppm quaternary ammonia. New sanitizing solution buckets were made and tested at 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)
